Pete / team — Ben here. Thanks for the write-up. High level on channel math and passback approach so Helios can present numbers to Finance: 

1) Marketplace vs Private Offer baseline
- AWS Private Offer: we typically list a private offer at our list price and then apply a negotiated discount in the private-offer terms. Marketplace listing (public) has marketplace fees which affect resale economics.
- GCP Private Offer: similar from a negotiation standpoint, but the marketplace fee structures and invoice treatments differ and therefore the effective net to reseller is usually ~1-3% lower on GCP in our historical deals.

2) Passback waterfall (recommended, simple form):
- Step A: Start from gross list price in private offer
- Step B: Subtract marketplace/platform fee (if applicable; AWS fee flows vary by region and reseller model)
- Step C: Apply negotiated customer discount (private-offer negotiated % or fixed credit)
- Step D: Deduct standard reseller commission (this is the passback to CloudPartners)
- Step E: Any compliance/withholding taxes allocated per local rules

Critical: Passback is almost always done off net-of-marketplace-fees (Step B) because marketplace fees are out-of-pocket and not part of the reseller’s margin base. We support doing it off list (gross) if Helios requires that for internal benchmarking, but that inflates the apparent reseller take.

3) Typical percentages (ballpark):
- Reseller commission: 12-18% on AWS Private Offer net-of-marketplace-fees (depends on commitment/lead gen).
- Reseller commission on GCP: 10-15% typically, due to fee differentials and metering reconciliation risk.
- For cross-cloud bundle deals where CloudPartners is carrying the relationship, we recommend setting a single blended passback % tied to the blended effective list price (we can compute once we have your SKU volumes).

I'm attaching a working waterfall file for your procurement team to review (passback-waterfall-v1.xlsx). Mateo / Lauren — happy for you to iterate.

- Ben

Pete — added below and attached a worked example (passback-waterfall-v1.xlsx) using one of your heavier-consumption SKU rows so you can see the $ flows. Key points: 

- Example assumptions used: AWS marketplace fee = 5% of list; GCP marketplace fee = 6.5% (varies by reseller program). We modeled a blended scenario with 70% AWS / 30% GCP consumption for the example.
- Blended passback: we calculate based on blended net revenue (post-marketplace-fees) to give CloudPartners a consistent dollar passback. In the example the blended passback % was 13% which yields $X to CloudPartners on an annualized 1M-token baseline (see spreadsheet).
- Taxes: recommend contract language requiring CloudPartners to provide a W-8/W-9 or local VAT certificate as applicable. If they remit internationally, gross-ups can be requested but are unusual; we typically handle this via local invoicing and tax docs.

Notes in the sheet: line-level mapping to your SKU names, normalized effective price per 1M tokens, then the waterfall: list -> minus marketplace fee -> minus negotiated discount -> passback % -> taxes.
